before.existing_compacted_memory: Bob (2 VP) has completed the road to N3 (Wheat Port Wh2) to leverage high Wheat production (N43). Goal: Settle N3 (needs 1B, 1S). Alice and Charlie (3 VP each) maintain a porous blockade, trading selectively to enable Charlie's N7 (B2 port) build while excluding Bob from Brick trades. Charlie has one hidden Dev card and a revealed Knight. Bob's B6 production (H5) is currently open, but Charlie moved the robber to Alice's H4 (S8) to slow her down. Bob used a 4:1 bank trade to bypass the Brick blockade. Watch for Charlie's new Brick port utility.

existing_relationship_updates.note: Alice/Charlie: Strategic alliance confirmed; they trade to enable each other's settlements (N7) while excluding Bob.
Charlie: Betrayed the hard blockade to trade Wheat to Alice, prioritizing his own expansion over the pact against Bob.
Alice: Remains hostile, prioritizing blocking Bob's growth even when sharing negative effects of the robber.
Alice/Charlie: Alliance is strained; Charlie blocked Alice's Sheep (H4) despite their previous trade cooperation.

Alice/Charlie: Alliance further deteriorated; Charlie continues to block Alice's Sheep (H4) and refused her Wood-for-Bri

recent_notes_kept_verbatim.note: Settled Node 3. I now have the Wheat 2:1 port. My Wheat production at Node 43 (Wh9) and Node 12 (Wh?) will now be much more efficient for future builds. Next goal: upgrade to city or expand towards Ore.
I have 1W, 1B, 1S. Need 1 Wheat to settle Node 3. Roll 9 should have produced Wheat from Node 43 (Hexes 14, 18), but state shows 0. Proposing trade to Charlie.

relevant_chat.message: Well, since the 'dry' brick market seems to be the only thing you two can agree on, let's see if the dice have a better sense of humor than this alliance.
Charlie, you've got that fancy new port but looking a bit thin on the wheat to actually use it. How about two stacks of grain for just one of your bricks? Help me, help you.
Like I told Alice, Bob, the brick market is empty. I don't have any to trade.
If you won't trade, the bank will. It's a steep price, but I've got grain to spare.
The bank's rates are highway robbery, but at least the road is getting built. One step closer to making all this grain actually useful.
The road is down. It's a bit of a trek to the coast, but that wheat is going to start paying for itself soon enough. Your turn, Alice.
Alright, let's see if we can get some actual production going. I'm tired of Alice and Charlie having all the fun at 3 points.
A 9! Finally, some wheat to work with. Since you two are still being stingy with the sheep, I'll just let the bank take a cut. Highway robbery, I know, but that wheat port is calling my name.
Well, at least the robber is staying away from my hexes for once. Good luck dealing with that, Alice.
Don't get too comfortable, Charlie. That port makes you a much bigger target than I ever was.
Alright, let's see if the dice are any kinder to me than you've been, Charlie. I'd really like that Sheep 8 back.
Charlie, you've got that shiny new brick port and I've still got plenty of wood. How about we keep the wheels of commerce turning? My wood for one of your bricks?
I'd love to help, Alice, but I actually don't have any brick right now.
Well, looks like the brick market is as dry as the desert. Good luck everyone.
Let's see if we can get some actual production going. Good luck everyone.
A 4? I'll take the wood, thank you very much. Alice, it looks like that sheep pasture is still a bit crowded with the robber hanging around.
Enjoy the wood, Charlie. Just a shame your fancy brick port is staying so quiet lately.
Let's see if we can get these dice to cooperate for once. That robber has been making himself way too comfortable on my pastures.
I'm tired of that robber camping on my sheep. Since nobody is trading brick, I'll just have to start paving my own way to it.
I'm making progress, even if it's one brick-less step at a time. Let's see if the next roll actually favors someone without a port for once.

after.long_term_summary: Bob (2 VP) settled N3, securing the Wh2:1 port and access to S5/W12. This leverages high Wheat production from N43 (Wh9) and N12. The Alice/Charlie alliance has frayed as Charlie maintains a robber on Alice's H4 (S8) and refuses her Brick trades despite her Wood offers. Alice (3 VP) is expanding toward the coast/inland (rds [20,19]). Charlie (3 VP) has a Knight and one hidden Dev card. Brick remains scarce; Bob bypassed the market via bank trades. Future goals: Upgrade N43/N12 to cities or expand toward Ore nodes to capitalize on the Wheat port efficiency.

task_context.instructions: Compress old memories and relevant chat into one concise strategic memory. Preserve future-useful facts: current goals, next planned actions, confirmed board facts, known or likely opponent plans/resources/dev cards/trade tendencies, active negotiations, social commitments, and mistakes to avoid. Discard repeated, completed, impossible, vague, or superseded details. Do not invent facts; mark uncertainty clearly. Also extract only new meaningful relationship shifts from the old notes and relevant chat: trust changes, grudges, favors, threats, betrayals, promises, or emotional tension. Do not repeat existing relationship updates; leave relationship_updates empty if nothing changed. Target about 50% or less of the combined old memory length. Keep recent_notes_to_keep copied verbatim from the provided recent notes.
